summary: Epoll removal updates file->f_ep while the __fput fast path reads the same pointer without taking the epoll semaphore.

call_chain.evidence: Removal path clears file->f_ep when the last epitem is removed.
__fput calls eventpoll_release(file) early in file cleanup.
Inline fast path reads file->f_ep before calling eventpoll_release_file().
Full cleanup path is present in merged.ll after repair.

interleaving: epoll_ctl removes the last epitem for a target file and clears file->f_ep.
A final fput on the same file concurrently runs eventpoll_release() and reads file->f_ep as a lockless fast-path check.
The fix documents the intentional race with READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE on file->f_ep.

ground_truth_access.required_ordering: The fput fast-path read intentionally runs outside the epoll semaphore but must be marked against epoll's updates to file->f_ep.

vulnerability_surface.why_relevant: file->f_ep is the shared epoll hook pointer that lets both epoll_ctl removal and file finalization discover whether a file is linked to epoll state.

aliases.name: file->f_ep
aliases.evidence: struct file *file is taken from epi->ffd.file.

aliases.name: file->f_ep
aliases.evidence: __fput passes the struct file directly to the inline release helper.

aliases.name: head
aliases.evidence: head is assigned from file->f_ep before list removal.

thread_a.evidence: __ep_remove gets the target file through the epitem and updates its epoll hook pointer.

thread_b.evidence: __fput calls the inline eventpoll_release helper on the same file object.

allocated_by: attach_epitem allocates an epitems_head when file->f_ep is empty
published_by: attach_epitem stores head into file->f_ep under file->f_lock
invalidated_by: __ep_remove clears file->f_ep when removing the last hook
freed_by: free_ephead frees the detached epitems_head after unlink

coverage.analysis_conclusion: The confirmed interleaving needs eventpoll removal, the inline eventpoll_release fast path, and __fput as the file cleanup entry.

patch_hunks: 6474353a5e3d annotates file->f_ep stores in __ep_remove/attach_epitem and the eventpoll_release fast-path read.
indirect_edges: eventpoll_release_file repeatedly calls __ep_remove(ep, epi, true) for file->f_ep entries.
